findings.title: Async legacy writes derive from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: All four write paths (Create line 51, Delete line 110, Update line 135, DeleteCollection line 163) spawn a goroutine that does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` using the *request* context. The apiserver cancels the request context as soon as the HTTP handler returns, which in practice happens before or right after the goroutine starts. The derived context is therefore already (or immediately) cancelled, so the legacy store call will typically fail with `context canceled` and the legacy database will never be updated. Since mode 3's whole purpose is to keep legacy storage in sync as a safety net, this silently defeats the feature (errors are only recorded in a duration metric, never logged). Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (preserving user/identity values) as the parent before applying the timeout.

findings.title: Create records a legacy-storage duration on a unified-storage failure
findings.body: In `Create`, when `d.Storage.Create` fails the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `startStorage`. This attributes a unified-storage failure/latency to the legacy backend metric, so the legacy error rate/latency dashboards will show failures that never happened in legacy, and unified-storage create failures are invisible in the storage metric. It should be `d.recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`.

findings.title: Update records a legacy-storage duration on a unified-storage failure
findings.body: In `Update`, the error branch calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though the failure came from `d.Storage.Update`. Same consequence as in `Create`: legacy metrics get polluted with unified-storage failures and storage failures are not counted. Should be `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: Object name passed as the `kind` metric label in Delete causes unbounded label cardinality
findings.body: `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the object's `name` where every other call site passes `options.Kind`. Because `name` is a per-object identifier, each deleted resource creates a new Prometheus time series on the storage duration histogram, leading to unbounded cardinality and potential memory blow-up in both Grafana and the scraping Prometheus. It also makes the metric unusable for comparison with the other label values. Use `options.Kind`.

findings.title: DeleteCollection's legacy goroutine records a storage duration instead of a legacy duration
findings.body: Inside the background goroutine of `DeleteCollection`, the result of `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection` is recorded via `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ...)` with `startLegacy`. This reports legacy latency/errors under the unified-storage metric, double counting storage observations for delete-collection and leaving legacy delete-collection completely unmeasured. Should be `recordLegacyDuration`.

findings.title: Legacy Update is given the raw objInfo instead of the object already persisted in unified storage
findings.body: The previous implementation wrapped `objInfo` with `&updateWrapper{upstream: objInfo, updated: obj}` so that legacy storage persisted exactly the object that unified storage had stored. Now the original `objInfo` is handed to `d.Legacy.Update` from a goroutine. `objInfo.UpdatedObject` will be re-evaluated against legacy's own `old` object, which has a different resourceVersion than unified storage, so for PUT (which carries a resourceVersion) legacy updates can fail with a conflict, and for PATCH/apply the transformers run a second time against a different base producing a different result. The net effect is silent divergence between unified and legacy data – the opposite of what mode 3's legacy mirror is for. Additionally `objInfo`/`obj` are request-scoped values that are now read concurrently after the handler has returned, which is not guaranteed to be safe.

findings.title: Fire-and-forget goroutines have no panic recovery and no error logging
findings.body: Each write path launches a bare `go func()` that calls into the legacy store. If the legacy implementation panics (e.g. nil map, nil pointer in a legacy service), the panic is not recovered inside the goroutine and the whole apiserver process crashes – unlike the synchronous path, where the apiserver's handler-level recovery would convert it to a 500. The goroutines also discard the legacy error entirely (only `err != nil` is folded into a histogram label), so operators have no way to find out which objects failed to mirror. Add `defer recover()` with logging and log the legacy error with the object name/kind.

findings.title: Delete puts the base logger in the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: `Delete` builds `log := d.Log.WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)` but then does `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`. Downstream code that retrieves the logger via `klog.FromContext(ctx)` loses the name/kind/method values, making delete-path logs from the storage and legacy layers unattributable. Should be `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)` as in the other methods.

findings.title: NotFound from unified storage now aborts the legacy delete, leaving orphan legacy rows
findings.body: The previous mode 3 `Delete` explicitly tolerated `apierrors.IsNotFound` from unified storage and still attempted the legacy delete. The new code returns early on any storage error, so an object that exists only in legacy (e.g. created before the migration, or whose earlier async legacy mirror failed) can never be deleted from legacy via the API. These orphan rows will resurface if the deployment is ever moved back to a mode that reads from legacy (modes 0–2).

findings.title: Mode 3 integration tests assert legacy state immediately after k8s writes, which is now asynchronous
findings.body: The three new mode-3 sub-tests (file line 132, unified line 191, etcd line 287) run `doPlaylistTests`, which after creating playlists through the k8s client immediately queries the legacy endpoint `/api/playlists` and requires the same UIDs (line 523-531), and after each k8s update calls `getFromBothAPIs` comparing legacy DTO fields (line 547). In mode 3 the legacy write happens in a detached goroutine with no synchronization, so these assertions race against the background write and the tests will be flaky – and given the cancelled-context problem in the goroutine they are likely to fail deterministically. The tests need to poll/retry the legacy endpoint, or mode 3 must flush legacy writes before responding.

findings.title: Unit tests never verify (or wait for) the asynchronous legacy write
findings.body: All mode-3 write tests (`Create`, `Delete`, `Update`, `DeleteCollection`) assert only on the value returned from unified storage and return immediately; nothing calls `m.AssertExpectations`/`AssertCalled` or waits for the goroutine that performs the legacy write. The central new behaviour of mode 3 – that legacy is also written – is therefore completely untested (the cancelled-context bug above would not be caught). Worse, the goroutine may invoke the shared `mock.Mock` after the sub-test has finished; if the arguments don't match a registered expectation testify panics from that goroutine and takes down the whole test binary. Add a synchronization point (e.g. a channel closed from the mock's Run function) and assert the legacy call happened with the expected arguments.

findings.title: go.work.sum contains a duplicated entry and unrelated dependency churn
findings.body: The added block duplicates the line `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod h1:...` that already exists a few lines above, and inserts entries out of sorted order (grafana-azure-sdk-go after grafana/pkg/apimachinery). This indicates the file was hand-edited rather than regenerated with `go work sync`/`go mod tidy`; it is also unrelated to the dual-writer change and will churn/conflict with other PRs. Regenerate the file or drop these hunks from this PR.
